changes.headline: Freight halved on the Atlantic Aframax routes in the week ending Nov 6, while the Brent to WTI spread narrowed alongside it
changes.dek: Baltic Week 45: TD9 WS710 to WS397 (TCE just over $111,100 per day), TD25 about WS707 to WS399, TD28 $12.26M to $10.15M lump, TD15 WS633.75 to WS564.38, TD3C WS1262.5 to WS1220.63 (TCE $1,303,616 per day), TD22 to just below $58M. Gibson flash through Nov 5 pointed the same way (TD9 about $7.36 per barrel estimate basis). Brent to WTI spread $7.49 at Friday's settle, about $7.16 on Monday's tape. The weekly measures the week ending Nov 6, before Saturday's Gulf of Oman action.. The Baltic Week 45 weekly (week ending Nov 6, published Nov 9) shows the Atlantic Aframax complex halved in a week: TD9 (Covenas to US Gulf) fell from WS710 to WS397, TD25 (US Gulf to UK Continent) from about WS707 to WS399, and TD28 (Vancouver to China) from a $12.26 million lump sum to $10.15 million, with TD15 and TD3C easing more moderately. The Gibson daily flash through Nov 5 pointed the same way on a different basis, so the weekly confirms the flash's direction. Two disciplines apply: the weekly predates Saturday's Huda action, so it is not a reaction to the weekend, and the Brent to WTI spread narrowed to $7.49 at Friday's settle and about $7.16 on Monday's tape, with the flash's own read that the export arb stayed closed because the spread narrowed as fast as freight fell. Levels remain extreme in absolute terms. The Merey FOB discount, the confirmation gauge for the heavy complex, has no fresh print (last hard print Sep 22); no FOB narrowing is claimed without the print.
changes.balance_read: The freight leg of December's wide differential eased hard while the space leg did not, and the spread leg offsets the freight leg for now. December WCS remains a zero-lot mark at -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6); today's ICE file is its first chance to trade tighter into the easier freight, which is the test of which leg the front month is actually pricing.

changes.headline: The balance build has November and December running about 200 kb/d above the proven egress bound, with the overflow filling tanks toward working capacity
changes.dek: November: Alberta supply 4,508.3 kb/d, no maintenance offline, refinery demand 623.8 kb/d, exports capped at the 4,541.6 kb/d bound (maximum sustained shipments, proven by July 2026 actuals, applied from September), overflow +192.3 kb/d to tank, implied level 69.55 Mbbl. December overflow +215.9 kb/d, level 76.24 Mbbl. Working storage capacity 80.6 Mbbl. Marketable supply (reconciled leaves, ST3 through July): 5,357.7 kb/d for November.. On the current balance build (built Nov 4; AER ST3 actuals through September 2026, ST53 through August, ST39 through June), November supply runs at full rate with the fall maintenance season operator-confirmed complete, Alberta refinery demand is 623.8 kb/d, and exports are capped at the egress bound of 4,541.6 kb/d. Storage is the residual that closes the balance: October cleared with no build at 63.78 million barrels, November's overflow is +192.3 kb/d to tank (level 69.55 million), December's is +215.9 kb/d (level 76.24 million), and January adds +50.6 kb/d (77.81 million) against working storage capacity of 80.6 million barrels, the maximum observed ST3 closing inventory and a lower bound on true tankage. The storage figures are the model's implied residual, not a measurement. November Mainline apportionment is in effect (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert), Enbridge said Nov 6 the Mainline stays in apportionment for the foreseeable future, and December nominations close Nov 17.
changes.balance_read: This arithmetic is why December apportionment persists on the operator's own guidance and why the differential's December leg stays wide even as its freight leg eases: supply exceeds what egress can clear by roughly 200 kb/d a month with no maintenance relief in November or December. The legs are separating and price separately.

changes.headline: UKMTO confirmed two tanker events from Saturday evening, the mine mechanism stays unconfirmed, and the bridge proposal awaits a US answer with a presidential meeting today
changes.dek: UKMTO 199-26: tanker fire at 1920 UTC Nov 7, about 8 nm northwest of Khasab, crew evacuated, cause not stated. UKMTO 200-26: outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile at 2020 UTC Nov 7 in the strait, all crew safe. IRGC (Nov 7, 20:56 GMT): two tankers claimed on mines, plus a Fars third-tanker report, unnamed and unconfirmed, mechanism unclear per maritime press. Tape (Reuters, 1134 GMT Nov 9): Brent Jan27 $97.67 (-0.6%), WTI Dec26 $90.51 (-0.4%) vs Friday settles $98.32 / $90.83. Trump meets the Qatari PM today 12:00 p.m. ET; told CNN Sunday new strikes are highly unlikely against a very strong agreement.. UKMTO Warning 199-26 records a tanker catching fire at 1920 UTC on Nov 7, about 8 nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman, with the crew evacuated; Warning 200-26 records a second, outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile at 2020 UTC while transiting the strait, all crew safe. JMIC retains a severe threat assessment. The IRGC announced at 20:56 GMT on Nov 7 that two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire, and Fars later reported a third tanker explosion; no vessel is named in either claim, Reuters was unable to confirm the mine strikes, and it remains unclear whether the reported explosions were caused by mines, missiles or drones. The confirmed and the claimed stay in separate columns: the events are confirmed, the mechanism is not. The Qatari two-day bridge proposal stands (day one: blockade lifted and part of about $8 billion released against IAEA inspections; day two: the strait reopens via the Oman route), Tehran says it awaits Washington's answer, Qatar denies the talks failed, and the US president meets the Qatari prime minister today at 12:00 p.m. ET. Monday's tape was choppy and modestly lower, Brent $97.67 and WTI $90.51 on the latest Reuters snapshot, inside ranges of $96.91 to $98.35 and $89.85 to $91.30.
changes.balance_read: Saturday's enforcement and the confirmed tanker events raise the risk price of transiting the corridor, while the proposal gives the de-escalation branch a priceable shape with a day-two reopening. Neither changes a confirmed crude barrel count: the disabled vessel carried no crude, and the tankers' cargoes and damage are unassessed. The dated verdicts are today's meeting readout, Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, and Thursday's inventory print.

flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, the balance shows about 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. The registered December judgment call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack now includes the operator's Nov 6 statement that the Mainline is at or near capacity and expected to remain in apportionment for the foreseeable future, a balance build with November and December supply running about 192 and 216 kb/d above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a freight leg that halved in the week ending Nov 6, and a December differential that has still not traded tighter. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows the close and grades the call. Trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop before the nominations close

flags.title: Distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003: the products leg is the tight part of the US balance into winter
flags.detail: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. The validated diesel crack is $91.19. The Russian diesel arrangement has produced zero confirmed US discharges nearly a month after the Oct 9 deal: the first cargo's listed Nov 7 arrival lapsed with the vessel signalling for orders, and Russia has extended its producer diesel export ban to Jan 31, 2027 (reported). The graded weekly balance scorecard shows the model's crude error channel runs through distillate. The next inventory report is Thursday Nov 12. Trigger: The EIA release at 12:00 p.m. ET on Nov 12, a distillate stock build back above 105 million barrels, or a diesel crack break in either direction

flags.title: Freight halved, the spread narrowed with it, and no arb reopening is confirmed: the two legs move together or not at all
flags.detail: The Baltic Week 45 weekly (week ending Nov 6) halved the Atlantic Aframax complex: TD9 WS710 to WS397, TD25 about WS707 to WS399, TD28 down $2.11 million on the lump sum, with VLCC rates easing more moderately and TD3C TCE still $1,303,616 a day. The Gibson flash through Nov 5 read the export arb as still closed because the Brent to WTI spread narrowed as fast as freight fell; the spread closed Friday at $7.49 and stood at about $7.16 on Monday's tape. The Merey FOB discount, the confirmation gauge for walked-down competitor offers at the Gulf, has no fresh print since Sep 22. Saturday's Gulf of Oman enforcement has no rate print yet: every dated freight print in hand closes on or before Nov 6. Trigger: A Monday or Tuesday rate print carrying the weekend's events, a fresh Merey FOB print, or a traded December WCS settle at tighter levels

forward_calendar.what: US president meets the Qatari prime minister, 12:00 p.m. ET
forward_calendar.detail: A closed-press Oval Office session on the two-day bridge proposal (blockade lifted and part of about $8 billion released against IAEA inspections, the strait reopening on day two). Any readout is the day's flat-price event; Tehran says it awaits Washington's answer and no acceptance exists.

forward_calendar.what: US-hosted Ukraine and Russia talks, Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11)
forward_calendar.detail: The trilateral round goes in against Kyiv's heaviest strike week of the autumn: 115 missiles and more than 3,000 drones in the week to Nov 8, six-plus Russian refineries struck since Oct 30 with the newest hits unconfirmed in extent. Kyiv wants a ceasefire first; the named gap is Russia's demand for all of Donetsk. Any energy ceasefire language is a products and differentials event first.

forward_calendar.what: EIA weekly petroleum report, 12:00 p.m. ET (delayed for Veterans Day)
forward_calendar.detail: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 is released a day late for Veterans Day. It is the first balance print after the repricing, and distillate at 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, is the line that matters; the graded weekly balance scorecard puts the model error channel in distillate.

The deadline for December shipper nominations. The registered December judgment call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows the close, with the balance showing roughly 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space into the notice.

forward_calendar.detail: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the fourth quarter capacity review setting the baselines for 2027 quotas.
